name: Shushing Face
baseMeaning: A yellow face with a finger pressed to its pursed lips, the universal gesture for 'shhh'.
tldr: 🤫 means keep it quiet, but it can also tease a private reveal or leave a flirtatious implication in a close chat.

contextMeanings.meaning: It asks the recipient to keep sensitive news confidential.
It teases that you know something and are waiting for the reveal.
It suggests a private or flirtatious thought that the two of you share.
It asks for discretion around company news, though it can also seem unprofessional or commanding.
contextMeanings.example: please keep the client news off the record for now 🤫

platformNotes.note: In a work Slack channel, 🤫 is most likely to be heard as “keep this off the record,” not as flirtation. Because it can still sound like a command to stay quiet, use it only when the request is appropriate.

In a private iMessage thread, 🤫 often closes an intimate aside or announces a secret the recipient should not share. The same emoji in a family group can still be read literally, especially by older participants.

On Instagram, 🤫 can work as a teaser that there is more to reveal. In dating conversations it takes on a more suggestive meaning, while a public caption may leave some of that implication for people to work out.
In a Discord direct message, 🤫 can play the lighter teasing role seen in other private chats. In a larger server channel, its literal request for quiet is easier to misread.

generationalNotes.note: Among younger senders, 🤫 often reads as flirtation or a tease before a reveal, with literal secrecy as one possible interpretation. It commonly works as a suggestive DM closer.
For 22–35-year-olds, the emoji has several common meanings: private gossip, tease-before-reveal, and flirtation. Literal confidentiality remains common in friend threads when real news is involved.
For 35–50-year-olds, 🤫 is more likely to be heard first as “shh” or “I have a secret,” though dating conversations can bring out its suggestive side. The literal interpretation can win by default.

warnings.title: Taken as a literal demand for quiet
warnings.description: Older recipients may ignore the teasing meaning and hear a formal request for silence. Say “please keep this between us” instead when the instruction needs to be unmistakable.

warnings.title: Unprofessional in a work channel
warnings.description: A manager or coworker may find 🤫 presumptuous, especially if the emoji stands in for a clear request. Spell out who can be told and why the information should stay private.

seoDescription: What does 🤫 mean? It can mean keep this secret, a teasing hint at a private reveal, or a suggestive aside in a dating chat.

longForm.overview:
🤫 shows a yellow face with a finger pressed to its pursed lips. The artwork still suggests silence, but the emoji now does more than ask people to stop talking. It can mark a secret as private, promise that a reveal is coming, or create a suggestive aside in a private chat. Around 2020, its use shifted noticeably from the plain “shh” toward teasing and flirtation, especially among younger senders.

Its exact job depends on the conversation. “Don’t tell anyone 🤫” asks for real discretion. “You know what I mean 🤫” to a date can imply that there is a private thought worth sharing. In a work channel, it may be taken as an instruction to keep quiet, which can look unprofessional or create the wrong impression. That makes context more important than the emoji’s innocent-looking face. It is also more deliberate than 🤭: 🤭 reacts to nearly saying something, while 🤫 deliberately withholds the thought or reveal.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🤫 fits the small moments around a disclosure: a friend shares a pregnancy, job offer, breakup, or piece of gossip and says not to spread it. It can also cap a tease before the person reveals what happened, or sit at the end of a private exchange like “thinking about you 🤫,” leaving the implication that something specific is being withheld.

In dating chats, 🤫 often says “I’m keeping this between us” in a more suggestive way than the words alone. That meaning is especially common in dating-app conversations and established flirtatious DMs. In friend threads, the same emoji is more likely to mark genuine confidentiality, especially when the news actually has a small audience.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🤫 when an older relative or colleague may take the finger on the lips literally. A daughter announcing a promotion with “keep this quiet 🤫” may be asking for discretion, but the emoji can still sound like a formal demand for silence. In a surprise-party plan, it may make an older recipient wonder what else is being hidden.

Work channels are the riskiest setting. A junior employee sending 🤫 to a manager can read as unprofessional or as an awkward request to keep a matter off the record. Use direct, respectful wording there: “Please don’t share this yet” or “keep this between us.” Outside dating, avoid using 🤫 as a vague substitute for a clear message.
longForm.howToReply:
Match a confidential 🤫 with 🤫 if you genuinely understand the secret and are willing to keep it between you. Two together can make the promise feel mutual. For a teasing or suggestive 🤫, 😉 gives a lighter “I see you” response, while 😏 can push the moment toward something more deliberate.

If someone sends 🤫 after your news, treat it as a good sign: they are keeping your reveal contained. If the emoji feels too cryptic, ask “what are we not saying?” rather than leaving the private joke hanging. In a work reply, acknowledge the request directly and confirm who can be told.

faqs.question: What does 🤫 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: In a dating-app thread, it is a strong sign of flirtation, suggesting that he has a private thought to share. In a friend thread, it is more likely to mean that he wants to keep the news confidential.

faqs.question: Is 🤫 flirty?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, especially in a private dating chat or a relationship with established flirtatious banter. It can also be completely practical when the sender genuinely has news to keep secret.

faqs.question: What does 🤫 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: In a caption or comment, it commonly teases that there is more to reveal or that the creator is not saying everything yet. Depending on the message, it can also mark a secret or create a suggestive aside.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🤫 and 🤭?
faqs.answer: 🤭 is reactive, like “oops, I almost said something,” while 🤫 is deliberate. Use 🤭 when something nearly slipped and 🤫 when you are intentionally keeping a thought or reveal quiet.

conversationExamples.message: ok i got the job 🤫 please don't tell anyone yet
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is genuine confidentiality. Acknowledge the news privately and confirm that you will not spread it before the sender announces it.
The emoji leaves a private, flirtatious implication, especially if you already share playful chemistry. Reply with 😉 or 😏 to match the tease, or ask what they are hinting at.

conversationExamples.message: please keep the client news off the record for now 🤫
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is asking for discretion, but the emoji can sound unprofessional in a work channel. A clearer reply would confirm who can be told and when the information may be shared.

conversationExamples.message: don't say anything about the surprise party 🤫
conversationExamples.interpretation: The literal request is clear, but an older relative may focus on the shushing gesture and wonder what else is being hidden. Reassure them that the secret concerns only the surprise.

conversationExamples.message: wait till i post the screenshot 🤫
conversationExamples.interpretation: This teases that more information is coming rather than making a serious promise of secrecy. Ask what the screenshot shows or wait for the promised reveal.
